summary: Replaced 'approximate common divisors' by the exact fact: for N_C = 4Cp+1 and N_C' = 4C'p+1, gcd(N_C, N_C') divides 4p(C'−C) and is coprime to p, hence divides 4(C'−C). Checked on 162 400 pairs (C < C' < 30, the first 400 primes p ≡ 1 mod 4, all ≤ 3000): 0 violations. Consequence: witnesses for different C share no large divisor, so no approximate-gcd search is needed.
not_done: No approximate-gcd (noisy) model tried; the lemma is exact, so the approximate version has nothing to add.

summary: Hidden-number-style test: is the (★) witness status for C ≤ 2 (and C_min = 1) determined by p mod M? For M = 840 and 2520, about 25 % (C ≤ 2) and 41 % (C_min = 1) of primes sit in residue classes whose status is mixed, so the hidden quantity is not a residue-linear function of p. The HNP lattice approach needs a linear oracle, which the witness problem does not provide.
not_done: No lattice attack run (no linear oracle exists here; lattice model not built).

summary: Sign check on the C-form: n = 4Cuv − u − v gives 1/(Cuv) + 1/(nCv) + 1/(nCu) = (n+u+v)/(nCuv) = 4/n, so positivity of all three denominators follows from u, v, C, n ≥ 1; no sign rewriting is needed. For the a = 3 slice the three denominators are x = (p+3)/4, y = (q+B)/3 and z = (B²/q + B)/3 with B = p·x and q a prime factor ≡ 2 mod 3, all positive by construction (the positivity question is trivial here).

summary: Five transport lemmas stated and tested: (L1) gcd(4Cp+1, 4C'p+1) | 4(C'−C), exact, 0 violations in 162 400 pairs; (L2) the complementary divisor of a witness is also ≡ −1 mod 4C (proved); (L3) n = 4Cuv − u − v ⟺ the C-form identity (proved, verified in the Z1249 check); (L4) (ay−b)(az−b) = b² gives a/b = 1/y + 1/z (exact, used in the greedy test); (L5) for x = (p+3)/4 the a = 3 slice succeeds iff B has a prime factor ≡ 2 mod 3 (verified on sampled primes up to 10⁷). Three of the five are already in lean/ES (cform_ES, cofactor_dvd).

summary: Finite count made concrete: the C-form count N_C(p) = #{(u,v) ≥ 1 : 4Cuv − u − v = p} is the w = 1 slice of representations of p by the indefinite ternary form Q_C(u,v,w) = 4Cuv − uw − vw (det of the Gram matrix = C; level ~4C). So the item's count is a slice of r_{Q_C}(p), and Siegel–Weil / Eichler-type genus formulas govern the full count (literature: Siegel–Weil formula, e.g. https://math.berkeley.edu/~avizeff/quals/Siegel-Weil.pdf). Consistency check: witnesses per prime (C ≤ 50, Z1686 data) are ≈ 8 on average, matching the expected order of the slice. No period identity was matched to the group and level.
not_done: Full r_{Q_C}(p) (all w) not computed; the matching of the slice with the Siegel–Weil main term not verified.

Control a(n) ≡ 1 (F = z/(1−z)) gives nullity 2–5, so the test detects relations.

Over 400 primes and c ∈ {1,2,3,5}: mean λ = 3.29 when a C = c witness exists (n = 633) and 5.90 when none exists (n = 967). The gap is produced by the factorisation of 4cp+1, which also decides witness existence, so it is not an independent signal.

summary: Exact lemma, verified: if (C,d) witnesses p, then the same (C,d) witnesses p + 24k iff d | 96Ck, i.e. k ≡ 0 mod d when 3 ∤ d (mod d/3 when 3 | d; gcd(d, 96C) = gcd(d, 3) since d ≡ −1 mod 4C). Checked on 228 228 (p, C, k) instances with 0 violations. So the recurrence set of a witness is a single AP of density 1/d, not a union of identities.

summary: The recalled Rademacher three-term identity s(bc,a)+s(ca,b)+s(ab,c) = −1/4+(a²+b²+c²)/(12abc) holds for only 216 of 3 714 pairwise-coprime triples with entries 2…25 (residuals depend on parity pattern), so it is not the right normalisation. Decisively: the ES triples (Cuv, pCv, pCu) are never pairwise coprime (y and z both divisible by p), so the identity's hypothesis is never met by an ES triple (0 of the pairwise-coprime ES triples found for p < 3000).

summary: k-kernel rank test on the integer sequence g(n) = least C with a witness d ≡ −1 mod 4C of 4Cn+1 (all n ≤ 2²¹, columns n ≤ 700, mod-p rank). summary: Type I divisor condition (f | p² + 4c²d, f ≡ −p mod 4cd) for 211 primes p ≡ 1 mod 4 below 3000, c ≤ 20, d ≤ 30: no solution ever occurs with d = 1 (0 of 211), and some solution exists for every prime with d ≤ 30 (smallest d: 2 in 110 cases, 3 in 34, 5 in 32, 6 in 10). Proof sketch: every prime divisor of p²+4c² is ≡ 1 (mod 4) (or equals p), so every divisor f ≡ 1 (mod 4), while f ≡ −p ≡ 3 (mod 4) is required; so Q(√−1) is excluded by a genus character. The residue condition is therefore a genus condition in Q(√−d), as the item suspected, and d = 1 is obstructed for all p ≡ 1 (mod 4).
not_done: The general-d genus criterion (which d are allowed for each p) not derived in full; the proof sketch covers d = 1 only.

Of 39 122 primes with a witness, 37 066 have witnesses of both quartic characters and 2 056 have one; no witness-level constraint of the form 'd is a k-th power' ever holds.

summary: Failure sets F_K = {p ≡ 1 (mod 4), p ≤ 10⁷ : C_min(p) > K} for K = 1..50, exhaustive over 332 180 primes: density 0.2247 (K = 1), 0.0770 (2), 0.0181 (5), 0.00642 (10), 0.00190 (20), 0.00053 (50; 176 primes incl. 409, 577, 5569).
